title: Rio Grande LNG: 7,500 workers now. About 700 after 2027.
text:
Federal regulators approved a peak of 7,500 workers building Rio Grande LNG near Brownsville, around the clock. Once the plant runs, its developer expects about 700 permanent jobs. Housing and services built for the peak won't all have a buyer in 2028.

title: We watched Starship get caught by the tower
text:
On Nov 13 we stood on the beach across from Starbase and watched Starship launch. The booster was lost; 22.5 hours later the Ship came home and the tower caught it, a first. The bigger story is on the ground: land deals, highways, water plants and tax breaks reshaping the Valley.

title: Brownsville's ship channel is now 52 feet deep
text:
This summer the Brownsville Ship Channel was deepened from 42 to 52 feet, deeper than Houston's main channel. Bigger ships mean more cargo, and more cargo means warehouses, trucking and logistics jobs that outlast any one construction project.

title: $3.2B shipyard, 10,000 jobs? A projection, not a payroll
text:

text:

title: SpaceX is spending $986M at Starbase
text:
Two projects drive the next wave at Starbase: GigaBay, a $506M Starship factory, and a $480M launch expansion with two new pads. Each is expected to bring about 500 jobs, and SpaceX says at least a quarter will go to local hires.

title: Building near the Port of Brownsville? Ask this first
text:
That many workers need places to sleep, eat and park, but about three-quarters of the LNG workforce already lives in the Valley. Construction crews rent short-term; permanent workers buy homes. Before you build, ask whether your demand is tied to a construction schedule or a payroll.

title: The Valley's power grid: "the end of the line"
text:
ERCOT has long treated the Lower Rio Grande Valley as a constrained pocket, fed by long 345 kV lines from the north with no new generation planned. Its study found potential reliability problems once Valley peak demand reaches about 3,200 MW. For big plants and big subdivisions, that matters.

title: Starbase: 3,400 workers and 21,400 indirect jobs?
text:
SpaceX reported more than 3,400 workers at Starbase, and Cameron County's judge said the company signaled about 4,000 more this year. The county also estimates about 21,400 indirect jobs tied to SpaceX. Estimates are worth checking, but they show how much of the economy orbits a few employers.

title: Starbase workforce: 300 to 3,400+
text:

title: Port of Brownsville cargo doubled in five years
text:

title: SpaceX has options: $100B in Louisiana
text:

title: Investing near Starbase? Know the risks
text:
Starship is still a test program: in two days we saw a booster lost and a ship caught. Much of the Valley's boom depends on one company, the road won't be wider until around 2030, and the water projects depend on SpaceX's payments arriving on schedule.

title: Brownsville's plan to cut its reliance on the Rio Grande
text:
SpaceX's payments to Brownsville fund a wastewater reclamation plant (about 8 million gallons a day) and a water plant expansion (about 10 million more). The city uses about 21 million gallons a day, 70% from the Rio Grande. The mayor says the deal could reduce or even end that reliance.

title: Underwriting near Starbase? Ask these three questions
text:
A thousand-plus new jobs need homes in a market where homes cost less than half the state median. Before you underwrite: How much of your demand depends on Starbase? What's the water and road timeline for your site? What happens to your numbers if launch schedules slip a year?
